title: The Hinterkaifeck Axe Murders
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the unsolved 1922 Hinterkaifeck murders in Bavaria, in which six members of the Gruber family and their maid were bludgeoned with a mattock at a remote farm near the village of Kaifeck. They describe the family's unpopularity, the eerie events leading up to the killings (a fleeing maid, footprints in snow, a tampered lock, missing keys, a strange newspaper, attic footsteps), the discovery of the bodies on April 4, the forensic details, and the suspects, including neighbor Lorenz Schlittenbauer and Carl Gabriel. They cover the police investigation, the lost evidence, a 2007 police academy study, and a listener mail story about a squirrel hunt. The episode opens with pronunciation banter and closes with a Steve Guttenberg tangent and listener mail.

segments.title: Halloween bonus episode and pronunciation banter
segments.summary: The hosts introduce a creepy bonus episode about an axe-murdered family and joke about pronouncing the German names and place names correctly.

segments.title: The Gruber family and the farm at Hinterkaifeck
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the Gruber family who lived at the Hinterkaifeck farm near Kaifeck in Bavaria, their isolation and unpopularity, the abuse rumors, and the incest rumor about Josef.

segments.title: Maid quits and eerie events on the farm
segments.summary: A maid leaves, citing a haunting and attic noises. Footprints lead to the house with none leaving. A shed lock shows tampering, keys go missing, and a strange newspaper appears on the porch.

segments.title: Squarespace and Google sponsor read
segments.summary: Sponsor read for Google and Squarespace small business websites and email.

segments.title: Discovery of the bodies on April 4
segments.summary: A new maid starts March 31, the last day the family was seen alive. Neighbors check on the farm after the family misses church and the post piles up, finding the Pomeranian tied up and then the bodies in the barn and house, all bludgeoned and covered with hay or sheets.

segments.title: Forensics and signs the killer stayed on the farm
segments.summary: Doctor Mueller's autopsy identifies a mattock as the weapon. Cazilia had clutched tufts of her own hair, suggesting she survived for hours. The farm showed signs of recent meals, smoke, and fed animals, suggesting the killer stayed for days. Robbery is ruled out because valuables were left behind.

segments.title: Suspects: Lorenz Schlittenbauer and Carl Gabriel
segments.summary: Neighbor Lorenz Schlittenbauer, the alleged father of Josef, is a suspect due to his behavior at the scene and weak alibi. Carl Gabriel, Victoria's first husband who was reported dead in World War One, is also named as a suspect. The hosts discuss why each is or is not convincing.

segments.title: Later investigation and 2007 police academy study
segments.summary: Munich police decapitated the bodies for analysis, and the heads were later lost. Over a hundred suspects were interviewed. A 2007 study by a police academy student group concluded they knew the killer but did not name the person.

segments.title: Steve Guttenberg tangent and listener mail: squirrel shooting
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Steve Guttenberg and Party Down, then read a listener's story about shooting a squirrel with a pellet gun at age thirteen and deciding never to hunt again.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and give contact and website information.
